status: confirmed implementation gap; no CSS/template support claimed

legacyBehavior.finding: Styles are CSS files in Application Support/<CFBundleName>/Styles; style names may include the css extension; nil selects no base stylesheet.
Startup copies bundled Styles and Themes only when missing, preserving user edits and existing files.
HTML preferences select none or a discovered CSS filename, reveal the styles folder, and reload styles plus the preview.
Original htmlStyleName default is GitHub2; htmlTemplateName defaults to Default.

Preview uses the selected base CSS plus independently enabled code/diagram CSS. Styled export embeds base CSS; highlighting is controlled independently. Template is loaded from bundle/Templates and cached once, and receives title/titleTag/styleTags/body/scriptTags.
Asset options choose omitted, embedded or fully linked output. Embedded local asset content is read as text.

template.bodyPlacement: Rendered body is a direct child of body, without a main wrapper.
template.discoveryLimit: Observed original code loads templates from the application bundle; no user-template directory/import UI was found in the inspected renderer and HTML preferences.

currentBehavior.finding: Portable style input currently contains native typography/width/code-theme values; no selected CSS catalog or custom CSS snapshot.

Document shell is typed Swift and places content in main#preview-content; style updates replace CSS text without replacing content nodes. CSP disables document scripts/connect/frame/object/base/form execution and restricts resources.
DocumentStyle captures native appearance fields. Original htmlStyleName/htmlTemplateName values are not consumed by this adapter.
Persisted old keys are copied without overwriting current keys, but copying alone does not implement their behavior.
Fresh source/options/style snapshots feed typed PreviewHTML. Style export and code-highlighting options are separate; no CSS/template selection enters the export snapshot.

Local resource reader already permits CSS/font/image types inside the document directory, with descriptor-based symlink checks and bounded reads. It does not provide a separate imported-style asset root.

implementationRequirements: Retain the current liked Snowfolio notebook appearance by default. Make legacy/custom styles explicit selectable choices and distinguish existing Snowfolio appearance from imported legacy choices.
Restore all six original CSS assets with preserved bytes/notices and custom CSS discovery/import/reload, stable IDs and deterministic precedence for edited legacy files.
Provide an explicit no-document-styles choice independent of code/math/diagram styles and styled/plain export controls.
Preserve author CSS selectors, including body-child selectors. Appending legacy CSS over notebook CSS plus an extra main wrapper is not equivalent to the old document structure.
Use one immutable resolved presentation snapshot for preview, fresh HTML export, PDF and printing, including changes while automatic preview is manual.
Keep native style changes from replacing content unnecessarily; validate source/selection/scroll and math/diagram/code behavior.
Keep custom CSS as CSS data in initial shells and later isolated-world updates; a closing style tag must not introduce document markup or executable code.
Explicitly model relative CSS/image/font/import resources, export portability, allowed roots and lifetime. Do not broaden the existing document resource boundary silently.

Replace Handlebars assembly with Swift context/escaping and a documented compatibility adapter; characterize original bundled expressions first and make unsupported custom expressions visible rather than silently altering output.
Preserve default template title/stylesheet/body/script ordering while retaining the modern script-free preview/export pipeline. Compatibility must not reintroduce obsolete runtime JS.
Keep original renderer/preferences/template dependencies until both CSS and template consumers reach verified parity; retain all notices after implementation retirement.
